faq.answer: It's a tool that fetches a URL the same way social media crawlers do, reads its Open Graph (og:*) and Twitter Card (twitter:*) meta tags, and shows you exactly how the link preview card will look when shared on platforms like Facebook, X, LinkedIn, and KakaoTalk.

faq.question: Why does my link show the wrong image or no image at all?

faq.answer: Facebook, X, and other platforms cache the scraped Open Graph data. If you changed your tags after the link was already shared, you may need to use that platform's own cache-refresh tool (e.g. Facebook Sharing Debugger's 'Scrape Again') to force it to re-fetch.

faq.answer: No. We fetch the page on the server only to read its meta tags for your analysis — nothing is stored or shared.

faq.answer: Many sites render different content for real visitors than for crawlers. We send a social-crawler user agent (like Facebook's) so you see the same Open Graph tags that Facebook, X, and other platforms actually see.
